next_step: Finalize SLAs + sign MSA; legal to review GPU reserve clause
notes:
Summary: enterprise procurement for Dedicated capacity focused on strict throughput guarantees and predictable unit economics. Primary contact: CTO (A. Morgan). Confirmed need for sustained throughput and headroom for ad-auction spikes.

Highlights / requirements (asked on 2025-03-05 call):
- Workloads: real-time chat for end-user assistants (median response 60-200 tokens), reranking pipeline for auction-time ranking (100-800 tokens), nightly embeddings indexing (batch).
- Throughput guarantees: negotiating a minimum sustained throughput of 2,500 tokens/sec across reserved pool during business hours (09:00-18:00 PT). Prefer contract language that defines sustained window (8hr rolling).
- Burst policy: headroom for bursts up to 4,500 tokens/sec for 15 minutes (credit bucket model). Wants explicit burst credits and a recharge rate.
- Concurrency caps: prefer soft cap at 256 concurrent requests for low-latency tier; hard cap at 512 for background/batch routings. Circuit-breaker behavior must be documented.
- Latency SLOs: p95 latency < 120ms for responses <=256 tokens; p99 < 300ms. For reranking (multi-candidate) target p95 < 250ms. Require per-model and per-route SLO reporting in Console.
- Reserved GPU planning: baseline recommendation from Redwood SE: 6x H100 (80GB) nodes to meet targets with 20% safety headroom; alternative 12x A100S fleet with autoscale pods for batch indexing. Customer prefers H100s due to peak concurrency.
- Model routing & fallbacks: must support automatic fallback to smaller quantized variant (e.g., 7B quantized) when sustained load exceeds guaranteed throughput; routing policy must maintain availability for critical user flows.
- Cost & commercial asks: fixed monthly fee covering reserved GPU capacity + per-token surcharge for bursts beyond credit bucket. Customer asks for capped overage rates and volume discount after 6 months.
- Compliance: VPC/private control plane, customer-managed KMS, audit logging retention 2 years, EU data residency for EU traffic.

Timeline & recent activity:
- 2025-01-10: inbound form -> initial qualification. Owner assigned (Samira).
- 2025-01-22: discovery call (ff_2025_01_22_4420) - high-level requirements captured.
- 2025-02-18: deep technical workshop with infra & security (ff_2025_02_18_7741). Reviewed KMS and network architecture.
- 2025-03-05: SLA & throughput negotiation call (ff_2025_03_05_9082). Discussed burst credit model and GPU sizing.
- 2025-03-10: Redwood SE submitted draft capacity plan and cost model (drive://redwood/praxis_proposal_v2.pdf).
- 2025-03-12: legal requested explicit language on SLA credits and incident response (INF-3214 opened).

Open technical discussion items (detailed):
1) Definition of 'sustained throughput'—customer insists on 8-hour rolling average. Redwood needs to confirm measurement method (tokens/sec aggregated at pool-level, sample intervals).
2) Burst credit accounting—how credits accumulate during off-peak; how long credits persist; billing model for consumed burst credits.
3) Concurrency enforcement—soft vs hard caps; preferred behavior is queueing up to soft cap with backpressure and 429 after hard cap. Need Redwood to supply backpressure headers and retry guidance.
4) Model variant SLAs—customer wants guaranteed availability for primary model and documented latency differential for fallback variants.
5) Escalation & remediation—service credits calculation for SLO misses (sliding scale tied to severity, e.g., 2% monthly credit for p99 breaches beyond threshold). Legal wants explicit examples.

POC / evaluation plan:
- 3-week POC: run production-like traffic replay (traffic file provided) against dedicated pool sized per SE plan. Validate sustained 2,500 tps for 8-hour window and bursts to 4,500 tps for 15m.
- Observable metrics: per-route tokens/sec, request concurrency, p95/p99 latencies, GPU utilization, KV cache hit-rate. Redwood to grant access to Console dashboards for customer's ops team.
- Success criteria: POC demonstrates sustained throughput within 10% of target, latency SLOs met for primary model, burst policy behavior matches spec.

Commercial negotiation notes:
- Customer is price-sensitive; expects committed ARR ~ $200k first year with an option to scale.
- Asks for 12-month term with quarterly throughput review and right to scale reserved pool up/down with 30-day notice.
- Wants clear overage caps and predictable burst billing (prefer token-based capped overage rather than per-minute compute).

Next steps (short):
- 03/14: Redwood legal to provide MSA draft with explicit SLA credit formula (owner: Samira).
- 03/18: SE to finalize H100 vs A100 sizing with cost delta (owner: Evelyn).
- 03/20: Schedule POC kickoff; get IP allowlist and KMS test vectors from customer (owner: Marco for onboarding).

Notes from customer quote: "We need predictability more than lowest price — if you can guarantee sustained throughput and a sane burst model, we can commit."

Risks: slower-than-expected KMS integration, legal standoff on SLA credits, disagreement on measurement windows for sustained throughput.

Internal asks for Redwood team: prepare a short appendix showing sample SLA credit calculations for p99 and sustained throughput misses + a proposed burst-credit policy example (recharge rate = 10% of baseline per hour off-peak).
